# Data table

Many records in one view, with search, filters, sorting, column choice, selection and paging.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill odv-pill-out">Left out of Multi-brand</span> Multi-brand draws on core, content and media families, not data. It avoids tools staff use all day and points those to Dense data. <span class="odv-instead">Use instead: <a href="./card">Card</a>, <a href="./tabs">Tabs</a></span></p>

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** People find, compare and act on many records, often in bulk.
- **Not when:** A handful of rows (a plain table), or items people browse rather than compare (cards).

Instead:

- [Table](./table.md): A few rows, no tools.
- [Card](./card.md): Items to browse, not compare.

## How Multi-brand uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A number in a table</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> type.body</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A mono font</div></div><div class="cap">Prices sit in sentences and offers, not in columns to compare, so a mono font adds nothing in any brand.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A selected row or item</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> color.surface.selected (from the brand)</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A fixed blue</div></div><div class="cap">Selection follows the brand color.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Table row height</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> size.row (comfortable)</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A compact row</div></div><div class="cap">Customers browse on phones, and compact rows are hard to tap in any brand.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">An action on one row or item</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Button ghost with a word</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> An icon alone</div></div><div class="cap">A word says what will happen.</div></div></div>

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Every tool and row action is reachable by keyboard. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It stays a real table with headers; sorting and selection are announced. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add data-table
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Data table reads 12 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Data table's tokens to change Data table alone.
